budget_items.what_was_said: The chair explained the storm water task force's goal is establishing a storm water utility, collected separately like the sewer commission, to fund storm water infrastructure improvements town-wide. No figures were given.

budget_items.topic: Tree removal fine, 922 Flat Hill Road
budget_items.what_was_said: The agent recommended the commission issue a fine for removing trees without a permit; a member suggested replacement plantings could be used in lieu of the fee.
The agent said it would be her recommendation to issue a formal violation fine if the property owner does not resolve the matter by the next meeting.
The agent asked the commission for about a month before providing concrete budget figures, citing unresolved issues with fund allocation since the office combined with land use.

decisions.decision: No vote needed on the 1147 Massachusetts Avenue violation; the agent will arrange a site inspection with the property owner and advise on required filings for the removed tree.
Applicant at 922 Flat Hill Road to tabulate and plot the removed trees on an updated plan rather than an immediate fine being issued.
Required plan revisions set for the Catales project at 189 Hemlock Drive: no enclosed porch, no new retaining wall, removal of the carport, and additional plantings, ahead of a site walk.

The four dead trees at 100 Hemlock Road may be cut with stumps left in place to preserve slope stability; no replacement plantings required given existing canopy, though understory plantings were encouraged.
The agent will continue bringing administrative determinations before the full commission while she becomes familiar with local regulations, rather than deciding them independently.
Commission will hold off on any formal violation or fine for 314 Highland Street until the property owner appears at the April 1 meeting.
Commission agreed to give the agent about a month before presenting concrete budget figures.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Conservation Commission opened with a resident's storm-water complaint that led into review of a related unpermitted tree-cutting and driveway violation at his property, then heard several notices of intent (Hickory Hills ADA dock/ramp, a new home on Flat Hill Road, an addition at Hemlock Drive, a DPW culvert replacement, and a floodplain-fill project), most of which were continued to April pending storm-water calculations, revised plans, or site walks. Along the way the commission discovered unpermitted tree removals at two more properties, ratified an administrative tree-removal determination at 100 Hemlock Road, discussed outstanding violations at Highland Street and Middle Lane, and planned an Earth Day event for April 22.

what_happened.line: The commission found unpermitted tree removals at multiple properties, including one already under review for a driveway violation.
Four pending hearings -- an ADA dock/ramp, a new home, an addition, and a culvert replacement -- were continued to April for missing storm-water calculations, revised plans, or a site walk.
The commission ratified, 4-0, an administrative determination allowing four dead trees to be cut at 100 Hemlock Road, with stumps left for slope stability.
A formal violation and fine for tree removal at 314 Highland Street was held off pending the property owner's appearance at the April 1 meeting.
A budget update for the land use/conservation office, combined with land use, was deferred about a month.

why_it_matters: Unpermitted tree removal and drainage violations found this meeting could lead to fines or required plantings at several private properties once hearings resume in April.
Four active building and infrastructure projects -- a beach dock, a new home, an addition, and a DPW culvert -- remain paused, affecting nearby residents and applicants awaiting permits.
A stormwater utility, discussed as a possible new fee collected like the sewer bill, is being explored town-wide to fund drainage infrastructure.
